messages:
laura_support: Customer has intermittent 503s and only gave us a generic request number from their app. They say they can't find the server trace id. Any quick repro guidance I can give them?

sam_eng: ask them to capture response headers (curl -i or -D -). the trace/req id we log is returned as a response header — easiest for root-cause.

laura_support: can you paste a minimal curl we can share? customer is non-technical but can copy/paste.

sam_eng: sure. short, copyable example (they should replace $KEY and endpoint if needed):

```
# save headers + body to files so we can inspect both
curl -s -D headers.txt -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}' -o body.txt
# then share headers.txt and body.txt (or paste header lines that include x-redwood-)
```

sam_eng: if they prefer a one-liner that prints headers to stdout: 
```
curl -i -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}'
```

laura_support: good. what header name should I ask them to look for?

sam_eng: look for any header starting with x-redwood- or x-request-id. typical headers we set: `x-redwood-request-id` and `x-redwood-trace-id` (customer may only see one). Example header line: `x-redwood-request-id: 01F3A2...`. Ask them to copy that full value.

laura_support: customer also uses our Node SDK — can they dump the SDK request id instead of curl?

sam_eng: yes — quick tips by SDK: 
- Node: set DEBUG=redwood* (or REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug) before running so the client logs the request metadata. Example: `DEBUG=redwood* node app.js` — look for lines containing `request_id` or `trace_id`.
- Python: set environment `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug` or enable logger `logger = logging.getLogger("redwood")` then reproduce.

sam_eng: if they're behind a proxy that strips headers you can also ask them to set an explicit request header on the client: `X-Client-Request-Id: <some-random-uuid>` — include that in the curl so we can correlate if the server doesn't echo our header.

laura_support: what exact info do we need from them to make a fast escalation?

sam_eng: ask for these items (copy/pasteable checklist):
- Time window (UTC) when the error happened (e.g. 2026-03-15T18:12:34Z)
- The full response headers.txt (or output of `curl -i`)
- Any `x-redwood-request-id` or `x-redwood-trace-id` values from headers
- SDK + version (e.g. node 0.14.2) or cURL version
- Endpoint path called (/v1/generate, /v1/chat/completions, embeddings, etc.)
- Minimal reproducible curl (exact command they ran) and request body size (tokens/characters)
- Workspace/Account ID and region if known
- Whether they saw consistent 503s or transient spikes and approximate frequency

laura_support: perfect. i'll send the checklist + curl snippet. anything else for private deployments/dedicated customers?

sam_eng: for Dedicated/Private also ask them to upload the local agent logs and include the node/pod name + GPU host timestamp. tell them we may need a debug bundle.

debug-bot: debug bundle created (internal): https://internal.redwood/debug/bug-1768459123-attach - if customer uploads headers + curl output we can attach it here. :mag: 

laura_support: thanks — i'll post back when they share headers.txt. :thumbsup:
